question: Which exact 3.101.043 Bluetooth allocator, paired free, stock buffer, timer, and external-queue entries are safe for target-private callers?
prototype_hypothesis: sub_C840C54 is the Bluetooth allocation wrapper; sub_C840C60 is its paired one-argument free wrapper and is also the queue cancellation free callback; sub_C7EAFBC creates a stock Bluetooth buffer; sub_C7EB270 and sub_C7EB33C add and cancel owner-local timers; sub_C7EB9CC queues and wakes an external Bluetooth FSM event.
callsite_evidence: sub_C7ECE30 allocates a 0x38-byte GAP state and a separate 4-byte receive slot through sub_C840C54, establishing the subsystem allocator and one-argument size ABI.
sub_C808244 grows an SDP attribute allocation and frees the old allocation through sub_C840C60; sub_C808648 likewise frees attribute nodes and their list owner through sub_C840C60.
Stock queue cleanup adapter sub_C7EBD40 moves its third callback argument from R2 into R0 and calls sub_C840C60, proving the exact cancellation callback must use the same paired free as bt_alloc.
sub_C7EAFBC contains the string BuffNew and initializes the stock buffer prefix from payload length and headroom supplied in R0/R1.

sub_C7EB270 contains TimerAdd and constructs a 24-byte owner timer record from the seven AAPCS arguments; sub_C7EB33C locates a timer handle, removes it, and releases the retained handle, record, and argument.
sub_C7EB9CC contains External, inserts the five-argument work item under the owner lock, and signals the owner semaphore when the external queue transitions from empty.
control_flow_evidence: sub_C840C54 and sub_C840C60 are adjacent Bluetooth wrappers around the generic allocation/free pair sub_C1F903C and sub_C1F8FF8. Exact 3.101.036 has the same adjacent allocator/free structure and uses one callable for bt_free and bt_queue_free.

The former bt_free candidate sub_C42F0C0 calls sub_C588980. Exact stock callers pass destination, zero, and size to sub_C588980, and the veneer accepts three arguments; it is a memset-like path rather than a free operation.
The former queue-free candidate sub_C42F0CC reaches generic NuttX free but is not the paired Bluetooth wrapper selected by stock queue cleanup. Promotion therefore uses sub_C840C60 for both records.
ownership_analysis: Allocations returned by bt_alloc and bt_buffer_new are owned by the caller until transferred to a stock queue/timer or explicitly released with sub_C840C60. A successful timer or queue submission transfers its argument according to the stock cleanup callback contract; cancellation must use the Bluetooth-paired free wrapper.
unsafe_assumptions: Static exact-IDB analysis proves the callable family and ownership flow; external module execution on an exact 3.101.043 device remains unprobed.
Timer and owner-local queue functions require a live Bluetooth FSM owner and the firmware lifecycle state expected by stock callers.
recommended_probe: On exact 3.101.043, allocate and free guarded blocks through the paired wrappers, then enqueue and cancel one Bluetooth work token while checking allocator guards, owner progress, and heap integrity.

artifacts.role: stock queue cleanup adapter proving the free callback ABI
